issues.legal_issue: Land allotted to a displaced person as compensation for land granted for gallantry does not qualify for the exemption from surplus-area computation applicable to the original gallantry-grant land.
material_facts: The original land granted to the landholder for gallantry was situated in territory he left after partition.

The land in which he was later assessed for surplus area was allotted in India under the displaced-person rehabilitation scheme, as compensation for his loss, rather than being the original gallantry-grant land.
The surplus land was allotted to other persons, who paid compensation to the landholder and took possession.
issues.conclusion: The rehabilitation land was different from the original gallantry-grant land and was not exempt from surplus-area computation under section 51A of the Pepsu Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1955. The judgment setting aside the surplus declaration on that basis was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 51A, inserted with retrospective effect, exempts the land granted for gallantry, subject to its stated conditions; it does not extend the exemption to different land transferred as compensation for that land. Sections 7 and 8 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 provide for determining and paying compensation, including through transfer of property from the compensation pool, which does not make that property the same as the displaced person’s original land. The Court applied Sailen Krishna Majumdar v. Malik Labhu Masih, 1989 Supp. (1) SCC 302, which rejected extension of the gallantry-land exemption to replacement land granted under the rehabilitation legislation. It distinguished Gurbachan Singh v. Puran Singh, AIR 1961 SC 1263, and also referred to Piarey Lal v. Hori Lal, AIR 1977 SC 1226.

predicates.surplus_area_determination: A proceeding determined whether land held by a person exceeded the permissible area.
predicates.original_gallantry_land_abandoned: The person left the original land granted for gallantry and no longer held that specific land.
predicates.replacement_land_received_as_rehabilitat: The land being assessed was transferred to the person as compensation or rehabilitation property, rather than being the original gallantry-grant land.

issues.definition: When a surplus-area determination concerns replacement land received as rehabilitation compensation after the original gallantry-grant land was abandoned, that replacement land is not exempt from surplus-area computation.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose rights are adversely affected by a writ judgment may seek recall and a hearing through a subsequent writ petition if that person was not joined in the earlier proceeding and had no opportunity to be heard.
material_facts: The allottees had received formal allotments of the surplus land, taken possession, and paid compensation that the landholder accepted.
The landholder later obtained a writ judgment setting aside the surplus declaration without joining the allottees, although the judgment affected their rights.
The allottees filed a subsequent writ petition seeking, among other relief, recall of the earlier judgment and a hearing; the landholder’s successor contested that petition.
issues.conclusion: The allottees’ subsequent writ petition was maintainable, and the earlier judgment could not bind them because it had been made without affording them a hearing. The Court set aside the earlier judgment and the Full Bench judgment that had reversed relief granted to the allottees.
issues.legal_principle: A High Court exercising plenary jurisdiction under Article 226 may review or recall an order to prevent miscarriage of justice and correct grave or palpable error. Natural justice requires an opportunity to be heard for a person whose rights are adversely affected. The Court relied on the Constitution Bench decision in Shivdeo Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1963 SC 1909, which upheld a subsequent writ petition by a person affected by an earlier writ order made in that person’s absence.

rule.if: writ_proceeding_challenges_prior_writ_judgment and prior_judgment_adversely_affects_nonparty and affected_person_not_joined and affected_person_not_heard

predicates.writ_proceeding_challenges_prior_writ_ju: A person brings a writ proceeding seeking relief from an earlier writ judgment.
predicates.prior_judgment_adversely_affects_nonpart: The earlier judgment affects a person’s rights even though that person was not a party to the proceeding.
predicates.affected_person_not_joined: The person whose rights were affected was not joined in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.affected_person_not_heard: The affected person had no opportunity to present their case before the earlier judgment was made.

issues.definition: If a prior writ judgment adversely affects a person who was neither joined nor heard, that person may use a subsequent writ proceeding to seek recall of the judgment and a hearing.
